note: What a host signs to let its own browser talk to nvoken directly. The host is the identity provider; nvoken verifies the assertion and never learns who the subject is. Minting happens in host backend code and never in a browser — the private key is the App's browser authority, and a page that holds it can mint any grant the ceiling allows.

signing_key.note: Base64 of the 32-byte Ed25519 seed and of the 32-byte public key. `public_key` is what `nvoken client-key create --public-key` registers; the seed never leaves the host.

serialization.note: Compact JSON with no insignificant whitespace, members in this order, absent members omitted. Ed25519 signatures are deterministic, so identical claims produce an identical token in every language — which is what makes `token` below a check rather than an illustration. A verifier parses JSON and does not care about order; this order exists so the four SDKs can be held to one byte-exact answer.

refusals.note: A mint helper refuses these rather than producing a token the runtime will reject, so a bad grant fails in the host's own tests instead of in a browser.
cases: blank or whitespace-padded sub, tenant_key, agent_key, or any claim over 255 characters
neither agent_id nor agent_key, or both
a lifetime of zero or less, or over maximum_lifetime_seconds
an ops entry outside browser_operation_ceiling, or a repeated entry
iss, kid, agent_id, or session_id that is not a well-formed id of its kind
ops omitted without an explicit request for the whole ceiling — not thinking about scope and wanting everything must not be the same request
